dedupe_keys.name: risk of flooding from surface water rofsw

description: Risk of Flooding from Surface Water maps where flooding may occur in England when rain does not drain away through the normal drainage systems or soak into the ground but lies on or flows over it. The Environment Agency produces it from national-scale modelling enhanced with compatible local modelling from lead local flood authorities. It is probabilistic and shows overall likelihood, not a single event, in three bands, high (at least 3.3 per cent, 1 in 30, a year), medium (below that but at least 1 per cent) and low (below 1 per cent but at least 0.1 per cent), for separate depth thresholds of 0 (extent), 0.2, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 and 1.2 metres; the wider product family also covers depth, speed and hazard. Coverage is England in British National Grid, revised as needed (record modified July 2026). Data can be downloaded by area of interest and format from the Defra Data Services Platform or used through a WMS visible from 1:50,000 scale, free under the Open Government Licence with no public access constraints. Caveats: it is a complex dataset with preview only at certain zoom levels, it represents risk not a forecast, and it does not model individual sewer networks. Simulation uses: pluvial flood hazard exposure of drainage, transport and other assets, climate adaptation and emergency planning. It complements the Agency's flood defence register (data-ea-aims-spatial-flood-defences).
